review.authority: Seven application build configuration declarations only; no framework config evaluation or build execution.

next: Both Next configs mutate process.execArgv at config evaluation to remove --js-float16array. Todox otherwise exports an empty NextConfig.
OIP imports defineBeepNextConfig and redirect generation, passes process.env and a repoRoot derived from import.meta.url, declares PWA source/destination and a separate webpack hook.

The reviewed OIP command sets NEXT_DISABLE_PWA=1 and requests Turbopack. Effective PWA behavior must be established from the imported helper; declaration of a PWA destination is not evidence it is written by this command.
vite: Three lab configs declare the React plugin and an absolute @ source alias derived from import.meta.url. Their server.host fields are development configuration, not evidence of a build-time listener.
Professional desktop adds a .ts-to-.tsx fallback resolver, a Lexical source transform, explicit chunk groups, installed dependency aliases and VITE_/TAURI_ environment prefixes.
No explicit build outDir appears in the reviewed Vite configs; output defaults remain owned by the installed framework rather than assumed from this review.
storybook: Command explicitly names storybook-static output and sets NODE_OPTIONS=--disable-warning=DEP0205.
Story selection includes resolved epistemic-ui stories, shared UI stories and graph-3d driver stories; inputs cross the app workspace boundary.
Static directories include installed emojibase data and shared brand assets. Addons, manager/preview configuration and story imports remain transitive inputs.
Config reads PORTLESS and PORTLESS_URL while constructing HMR options. Their presence in config evaluation is not proof they affect production artifact bytes.

semanticInputs: Application routes/components, static assets, config imports, package resolution and installed plugins/framework/runtime
Environment and process arguments, absolute alias roots and path membership
Generated assets, output/cache directory state, source maps and logs
Build-time imports or prerendering with possible external effects must be reviewed separately
remaining: Follow OIP helper and redirects, Storybook manager/preview/addons, and application import graphs for complete classification.
Resolve effective framework settings and actual output trees; inspect time/network/randomness and sensitive capture before candidate experiments.
No development server, production backend or deployment was started; no runtime or reuse claim.

review.authority: Source branch interpretation; plugin constructors and build not executed.
observations: OIP supplies PWA source/destination without an enabled override. Shared helper enables PWA only when NEXT_DISABLE_PWA equals 0; this command supplies 1, so the helper passes disable:true to Serwist initialization.

Disabling PWA does not omit the plugin constructor: makePwaPlugin maps the configured feature to withSerwistInit with its disable argument. No claim is made about all constructor or framework effects.
Bundle analyzer is enabled by ANALYZE exactly 1 unless explicitly overridden. OIP passes process.env and supplies no analyzer override.
Shared helper composes MDX, PWA and analyzer plugins in that order after base configuration and security headers.
Base config selects tsconfig.next.json, repository tracing/Turbopack roots, merged workspace transpilation and import-optimization lists, and build/dev filesystem caching defaults.
resolvedQuestions: Meaning of the recorded NEXT_DISABLE_PWA=1 value at the repository helper boundary.
remaining: Serwist/MDX/analyzer constructor and framework behavior, imported redirect function, actual file outputs and capture.
Ambient ANALYZE remains a semantic configuration input; passing process.env does not identify its actual runtime value.

limits: Original reviews retained verbatim with original revisions and scope.
Eight distinct source hashes and seven recorded command definitions match current files/census.
Only the original bounded static conclusions are reused; transitive frameworks, plugin execution, environment values and actual output remain unresolved.
No historical runtime evidence is renewed, no cache policy changes and no qualification promotion.
